findings.body: The new visualization receives empty columns and empty data regardless of the query response, so the table appears blank and users cannot inspect results.
findings.failure_mode: The feature rollout silently replaces working table output with an empty table.
findings.impact: The new visualization receives empty columns and empty data regardless of the query response, so the table appears blank and users cannot inspect results.
findings.root_cause: The feature-flagged branch wires a hard-coded empty table object instead of the `result` being iterated.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the current `result.data` and `result.meta` as `tableData`, derive columns from the actual query fields or metadata, and preserve the existing title/custom renderer behavior as needed.
findings.title: The table-widget rollout renders an empty placeholder instead of query results
findings.trigger: Opening any dashboard table widget for an organization with the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature enabled.
findings.verifier_reason: The patch at line 164-174 shows the feature-flagged branch passes hardcoded empty arrays: columns={[]} and tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}. The result variable containing actual query data is not passed, so the table will render blank.

findings.body: `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are returned by the early `!searchQuery.trim()` path and are displayed despite being declared in `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES`.
findings.failure_mode: The UI contradicts its own hidden-attribute configuration and exposes implementation metadata in the default view.
findings.impact: `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are returned by the early `!searchQuery.trim()` path and are displayed despite being declared in `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES`.
findings.root_cause: The hidden-attribute predicate was added only inside the non-empty-search branch.
findings.suggested_fix: Filter `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` from `sorted` before the empty-search early return, then apply the search predicate to the already-hidden list.
findings.title: Attributes marked hidden remain visible when no search is entered
findings.trigger: Opening the span attributes section with an empty search query.
findings.verifier_reason: The patch shows HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter is only applied inside the non-empty search branch (lines 65-68). When searchQuery.trim() is empty, the early return at line 62 returns sorted without filtering HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES, so hidden attributes like is_segment, project_id, received will be displayed.

raw_findings.body: The module raises a TypeError because DRF's Serializer class is not subscriptable, preventing the endpoint module—and potentially application URL initialization—from loading.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Application startup or endpoint discovery fails before any request can be handled.
raw_findings.impact: The module raises a TypeError because DRF's Serializer class is not subscriptable, preventing the endpoint module—and potentially application URL initialization—from loading.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch applies subscription syntax to a runtime DRF class that does not implement generic class subscription.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Define the serializer as `class BrowserReportSerializer(serializers.Serializer):` and keep any generic typing in annotations only.

raw_findings.trigger: Importing the browser reporting collector module during application startup with the standard Django REST Framework Serializer class.

validated_findings.body: Malformed reports are accepted with HTTP 200 and counted as valid browser reports instead of being rejected with validation errors.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Invalid browser payloads enter collection metrics and cannot be distinguished from valid reports.
validated_findings.impact: Malformed reports are accepted with HTTP 200 and counted as valid browser reports instead of being rejected with validation errors.
validated_findings.root_cause: Both mutually exclusive format-specific fields were made optional without enforcing that one format discriminator is present.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add object-level validation requiring exactly one of `age` or `timestamp`, while retaining the mutual-exclusion check.
validated_findings.title: Browser reports with neither timestamp nor age are accepted
validated_findings.trigger: A report payload contains all other required fields but omits both the working-draft `timestamp` and editor-draft `age` fields.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The validate_timestamp and validate_age methods only run when their respective fields are present. However, DRF field-level validators only execute when the field has a value. If neither age nor timestamp is provided, neither validator runs, but this is intentional per the spec comments - both fields are optional and the endpoint accepts reports with neither. The claim of a bug is ungrounded.

validated_findings.title: Negative browser-report ages are accepted
validated_findings.trigger: A browser report contains an `age` value below zero, such as `-1`, and omits `timestamp`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that negative age values are accepted is incorrect. While age lacks min_value=0, the validate_age method is only called when age is present. The spec comments indicate both formats must be supported. Without evidence that negative ages are invalid per the W3C spec, this is speculative. The timestamp field does have min_value=0, suggesting intentional difference.
